# Gotham Gay

Gotham Gay, also known as The Gotham Gay, is Argelys Samuel Oriach. Brooklyn-based performance artist, artistic director, and systems architect.

## Identity reference

## Dual-laboratory hub

## Biography

Argelys Samuel Oriach is a Brooklyn-based performance artist, artistic director, and systems architect working across performance, design, and structural engineering. He constructs language for the room, page, stage, and screen. As founder and artistic director at Wild Lake Studio, he scouts and develops multidisciplinary artists whose practices, like his own, span multiple forms. His central offering to artists is his undivided attention.

Born in the Dominican Republic, he was raised by a housekeeper and a facility maintainer, and learned in adulthood that his mother was a writer and his father a musician, though neither pursued their craft. His structural impulse emerged at age eleven when he taught himself 3D design software to draft his parents' dream home. An architect later used that exact file for actual construction. And in the wake of the 2008 financial crash, he applied to Phillips Academy Andover to consciously design the conditions of his own life.

A method actor trained in the Alexander Technique, he spent the next sixteen years treating his body, voice, and daily life as a single structural instrument. In 2010, he attended Northwestern University’s National High School Institute (Cherubs) theatre program, playing Nick in a stage adaptation of The Handmaid’s Tale. From there, he studied the mechanics of somatic weight, physical posture, and human attention by fully inhabiting roles across elite institutions, physical staging, and corporate infrastructure. He went on to obtain a bachelor’s degree in English from Wesleyan University, where he took extensive coursework in studio art and critical theory.

That foundation fueled a twelve-year trajectory building organic growth systems. During that period, he served as Cynthia Nixon’s social media manager for her 2018 campaign for governor of New York, later pivoting to architect sovereign digital frameworks from first principles. But he approached his corporate roles as an undercover durational performance. It was a calculated effort to build his life out of poverty while auditing how complex systems scale from the inside out. That performance cycle recently closed with an intentional return to his body, breath, and voice.

For fifteen years, he guided independent multidisciplinary artists, building the live production and physical carrying capacity that became Wild Lake Studio (Wild-Lake). Wild-Lake operates as a research laboratory inside Seven Eighty Three (Lab 783), a venture foundry that builds infrastructure and whole companies. Inside Lab 783, he architected BASALT, a deterministic 7.83 Hz acoustic calibration engine for lossless masters and live streams, and Apsis, a zero-commission publishing system built on universal Apogee and Perigee patronage tiers. He also cofounded Bullpen, a baseball coaching and swing lab, with his brother, player-coach Jordy Oriach.

As a writer, he applies this same somatic rigor to narrative through a maximalist, stream-of-consciousness style. He authored This Is Not a Love Story, a digital short written as a screenplay in prose form, and is currently writing a pilot, a one-act play, and his debut hybrid collection, Graduation.

Across every medium, he builds the underlying physical and digital mechanics. He lives and works in New York.

## Current practice
- [Systems architecture](https://seveneightythree.com/): Seven Eighty Three, also known as Lab 783. Independent systems design practice and venture foundry. Wild Lake Studio was created within it as its research laboratory.
- [Talent infrastructure](https://wildlakestudio.com/): Wild-Lake. Formal name: Wild Lake Studio. Independent talent architecture, artistic direction, and sovereign A&R studio operating on fixed retainers with 0% IP ownership and 0% revenue share. Created within Seven Eighty Three (Lab 783).

## Writing
[The Messiness of Becoming](https://gothamgay.com/beauty-salon/) is the first Beauty Salon essay by Argelys Samuel Oriach. It explores migration, identity, and finding a voice between cultures, homes, and creative forms. Publisher: Seven Eighty Three.

[This Is Not a Love Story (Yankees)](https://thisisnotalovestory.net/) is a short story by Argelys Samuel Oriach, also known as Argelys Oriach. It is a screenplay written in prose form. Publisher: Seven Eighty Three.

## Deployment order

The ordered deployment index is Seven Eighty Three, Wild Lake Studio, Universe API, BASALT, Apsis, BULLPEN, Communal Foundation, and This Is Not a Love Story. Canonical URLs and entity IDs are published in [Deployments JSON](https://gothamgay.com/schema/deployments.json).


## Deployed Systems / Infrastructure

- BASALT (https://basalt.fm): Deterministic 7.83 Hz acoustic calibration engine, lossless mastering console, live radio tuner (https://basalt.fm/radio), and technical specification (https://basalt.fm/spec).
- Apsis (https://apsis.club): Zero-commission direct-to-fan publishing and live broadcast architecture featuring Apogee and Perigee fan brackets.

- BULLPEN (https://bullpen.vip): Zero-commission coaching infrastructure, 120fps swing mechanics lab, and AI subscriber intelligence for verified MLB/MiLB players. Principal Systems Architect alongside Founding Player-Coach Jordy Oriach. Incubated inside Seven Eighty Three (https://seveneightythree.com).
